newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - THAI NEWSPAPERS - AUG 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - THAI NEWSPAPERS - AUG 13.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Japanese banks have pledged to maintain their credit lines with Thailand, lending crucial support to the $16-billion international rescue package put together on Monday. Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya and other officials met representatives of the 21 Japanese commercial banks that do business in Thailand but did not ask for any new loans. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- The Asian Games will be held as scheduled next year and there is no conflict among the organisers, the education minister says. Sukhavich Rangsitpol, chairman of the Bangkok Asian Games Organising Committee, says the Olympic Council of Asia is kept fully informed of the progress of preparations and fully supported Thailand as the host. (BANGKOK POST)

- In challenging Chavalit Yongchaiyudh to remove Interior Minister Snoh Thienthong, his deputy Chalerm Yoobamrung and Education Minister Sukhavich Rangsitphol, the opposition has underscored the dilemma that will hamper any plan by the prime minister to reshuffle the Cabinet. As Deputy Foreign Minister Pitak Indravitayanan says he believes Chavalit will reshuffle the Cabinet after the signing of the International Monetary Fund economic rescue package, the opposition says it is a matter of how, not when. (THE NATION)

- The weaker baht is expected to push export growth to reach the Commerce Ministry's target of 10 percent by the end of this year, according to Customs Department Director General Pridi Boonyoung. He says the country's export growth, after the flotation of the baht on July 2, will increase significantly. (BUSINES DAY)

- By the end of this year, the government expects to receive plans for the partial privatisation of seven major state enterprises, whose combined assets are nearly one trillion baht. A coalition government source estimates that privatisation over the next six months to one year will raise more than 100 billion baht for government coffers. Another private sector source puts the potential government income from selling parts of the state enterprises at 250 billion baht. (THE NATION)
